_what: Which command advances which stage, and what must be true before it can run at all. next_commands.py reads it.
_why: automaton.py --next knows WHICH unit is actionable and cannot say WHAT to run. This records that. It is data, not code - edit it when a tool changes.
_honesty: cmd:null means nobody has confirmed the command; the candidates are listed so the next person can confirm one instead of guessing. precheck is a one-line python test that must pass before the command is emitted at all - and a precheck is only added once a REAL failure has named the module. morph has one because a traceback named vidyut. The translate and entity stages do not, because naming their client library would be a guess, and a precheck that names the wrong module reports working stages as blocked, which is worse than having none.
_corrections: 2026-09-14.02 - the morph note in .01 claimed --commit was the missing piece. A 200-row trial disproved it: ling_kosha.py fails identically under --survey and --commit with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vidyut'. Corrected below. Also: every {db} is now quoted, because the repository path contains a space and the unquoted form split it into two arguments.

ocr.note: Four plausible entry points and no way to tell them apart from flags alone.

ingest.note: Pass the category explicitly; the tool's own hint is hardcoded from the document it was written for. IAST is produced here unless --no-iast is passed, which is why there is no separate iast runner.

segment.note: SUPERVISED - step one of five. Ingest the JSONL, diag_retire_check, graft if it refuses, retire. Use block_AR_phase2.ps1, which has the gates. driver:false because a loop would re-segment an already-segmented document into {code}_seg_seg.

classify.note: Three scripts, probably three different jobs rather than three ways to do one.

iast.note: There is no iast runner and there need not be: ingest_jsonl_fast.py takes --no-iast, so IAST is produced at ingest unless suppressed. A document short of IAST was ingested with it off, or before the feature existed. Re-ingest is the fix.

translate_en.note: Observed 2026-09-14: about $0.00016 per passage, median ~17s, with occasional 600s timeouts against 503s. Cost is negligible; wall clock is not. A row whose call fails is written empty and is picked up again on the next run.

translate_hi.note: Same tool as English. Hindi lands in translations_l10n at lang='hi'; English lands in passages.translation.

qa.note: qa_report reads, heal_lowqa writes, qa_scan is ambiguous.

entities.note: --retry-empty exists and is what made the maintenance runner exceed PT1H in September. Leave it off in a driver.

embed.note: --model and --list-models exist; the default is used rather than pinning a model nobody has read.

morph.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-14. The previous note said --commit was the missing piece. A 200-row trial disproved it: ling_kosha.py raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vidyut' at line 130 under BOTH --survey and --commit. morph is 0 of 48,823 because the dictionary is not installed in this interpreter, not because of a flag. The precheck above is what stops this command being handed out again while that is true. vidyut also ships its data as a separate download; --data-dir points at it.

export.note: export_mb01_html.py and export_mb01_md.py are document-specific and are not general answers.

book.note: One candidate, flags unread. 37 documents are READY for this stage, which makes it the cheapest large win once the command is confirmed.
